chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Barnet band details: no Southern tours, 'Strollin'' and the rhythm section
summary: The band never went below the Mason-Dixon Line; McGhee wrote 'Strollin'' and other pieces; he lists the rhythm section and Barnet's temper.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: He didn't go South, did he?
Charlie?
Yeah.
No, he wouldn't go South. He wouldn't go South. I had an incident there with Georgie Auld about that shit, though...
Well, we'll get to that later. But I guess Charlie was one of the White bands that played the Apollo, because I remember hearing him there.
Yeah, we played the Apollo several times. In fact, we played everywhere, except anywhere below the Mason-Dixon Line. We'd never go down there.
Did you go to California with him? Or didn't you get out that far with Barnet?
I don't think we went that far. We went out to St. Louis and and Minneapolis and places like that, but we didn't go to California.
Did you do any writing in the Barnet band?
Yeah, they got some. We even recorded...
Like that?
"Strollin'" -- that's my composition and my arrangement.
"Strollin'," huh?
Yeah. Charlie recorded it. Well, I wrote

"McGhee Special" -- I featured that with him, too. What else did I...? I had another thing there, too, that I keep trying to think of what it was. [SINGS 8 BARS] It's Duke's tune. I wrote it up for Charlie.
He loved Duke so much.
Yeah. Well, I figured he'd like that, and he did -- he liked it. But I can't think of the name of it.
I know the song. It sounds so familiar when you sing it. [SOUNDED LIKE TIZOL'S "MOONLIGHT FIESTA"]
Mmm-hmm.
Who was in the rhythm section in that band?
In Charlie's band?
Yeah.
Lew Fron, Chubby and what's his... A piano player from Boston.
Al Haig?
No, not him.
He played with him later, I guess.
No, this was a little fellow. He wrote for Woody a lot.
Oh, Ralph Burns.
Ralph Burns was the piano player in the band. And we had two basses.
Did you have a guitar player?
Yeah, Turk van Laek. I think it was Turk van Laek. In fact, I don't remember nobody else.
Because I know he had had a guitar inn the previous band, so I guess...
Who was that?
Bus Etrey. That was...
No, he wasn't on it.
No, I'm just saying that he had a guitar chair.
Yeah. But no, he wasn't in the band when I was in the band.
No, I know that.
I think it was Turk van Lake. In fact, I know it was Turk van Lake, because he's the one that got me the job with Georgie Auld.
Anyway, do you remember any incidents with Charlie other than his gambling? Because he had such a reputation as a wild man...

Heh-heh, oh yeah! He was kind of funny several times. But I mean, like, I didn't pay no attention. I mean, I know Charlie, that he didn't mean half the shit... He could turn red as a beet, but I mean, he didn't mean that shit, because the next minute he'd be all forgot about.No, we didn't have no incidents when we were running together about anything.
But I know wherever we played, Charlie didn't go for no bullshit about anybody being a color or whatever -- which was beautiful, you know. It's a bitch to be colored and have that shit bum you...
